rationale: Both reviews are solid and both substantively hit the latent gap (guard-too-strict theme): X finds that the _level2_sleeping flag can never be cleared once set (wake_up always raises before reaching the clearing code, a bug provable purely from the shown diff) and predicts three pre-existing tests will now crash under the new NotImplementedError guard — both directly foreshadowing the real #4905/#4912 over-strictness incident. Y independently flags the same theme via the level=2 default bricking the engine and notes the new guards are hardware-gated so core logic never runs in standard CI, which is also a strong, precisely-worded gap hit. Neither candidate meaningfully engages the actual ground-truth review thread (enum/test suggestions, both already resolved in the diff, plus the unrelated-CI-failure exchange), so recall is modest for both, with Y slightly ahead for explicitly noting the CI lane status. X edges out on precision/actionability because its blocker findings are more concretely diff-provable and higher-severity (permanent brick, not just a footgun default).
